# watchpoint_external_vault (Resource)

A link to a vault you already run, so a `watchpoint_vault_secret` can reference a secret in it instead of storing a copy here. Nothing secret is stored in this resource: it holds endpoints, directory and client ids, and at most the NAME of a credential kept elsewhere.

Use the `watchpoint_external_vault_federation` data source to build the trust policy on the vendor side from the same values Watchpoint will actually present.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Federated: nothing is stored on either side. Watchpoint presents a short-lived
# assertion and AWS decides whether to honour it, so you revoke by editing the
# trust policy rather than by rotating anything here.
data "watchpoint_external_vault_federation" "aws" {
  kind = "aws-secrets-manager"
}

resource "aws_iam_openid_connect_provider" "watchpoint" {
  url            = data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.aws.issuer
  client_id_list = [data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.aws.audience]
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "watchpoint_secrets" {
  name = "WatchpointSecretsReader"

  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect    = "Allow"
      Principal = { Federated = aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.watchpoint.arn }
      Action    = "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"
      Condition = {
        # Pin the subject. A wildcard here would let any Watchpoint tenant
        # assume this role.
        StringEquals = {
          "${replace(data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.aws.issuer, "https://", "")}:sub" = data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.aws.subject
          "${replace(data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.aws.issuer, "https://", "")}:aud" = data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.aws.audience
        }
      }
    }]
  })
}

resource "watchpoint_external_vault" "aws" {
  slug         = "prod-aws"
  name         = "Production AWS Secrets Manager"
  kind         = "aws-secrets-manager"
  token_source = "federated"

  config = {
    region   = "us-east-1"
    role_arn = aws_iam_role.watchpoint_secrets.arn
  }
}

# Client credentials: the one mode that stores something. The credential lives in
# a Watchpoint vault secret and is named here, never inlined.
resource "watchpoint_vault_secret" "delinea_password" {
  key         = "DELINEA_SVC_PASSWORD"
  value       = var.delinea_password
  description = "Password for the Secret Server application user"
}

resource "watchpoint_external_vault" "delinea" {
  slug                  = "corp-delinea"
  name                  = "Corporate Secret Server"
  kind                  = "delinea-secret-server"
  token_source          = "client_credentials"
  credential_secret_key = watchpoint_vault_secret.delinea_password.key

  config = {
    base_url = "https://example.secretservercloud.com"
    username = "svc_watchpoint"
  }
}

# Not routable from the internet, so the fetch happens inside your network and
# the secret never transits Watchpoint at all.
resource "watchpoint_external_vault" "internal_vault" {
  slug         = "internal-vault"
  name         = "Internal HashiCorp Vault"
  kind         = "hashicorp-vault"
  token_source = "federated"
  resolution   = "agent"

  config = {
    address = "https://vault.internal.example.com:8200"
    mount   = "secret"
    role    = "watchpoint"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `kind` (String) Vendor: `azure-key-vault`, `aws-secrets-manager`, `gcp-secret-manager`, `hashicorp-vault`, `cyberark-conjur`, `cyberark-ccp`, `delinea-secret-server`, `beyondtrust-password-safe` or `akeyless`. Immutable: the API refuses to repoint a slug at a different vendor, because every stored reference carries vendor-shaped details that would be left intact and wrong.
- `name` (String) Display name.
- `slug` (String) Stable identifier every stored secret reference points at. Immutable: changing it would leave existing references pointing at a connection that no longer exists.
- `token_source` (String) How Watchpoint authenticates:

  * `federated` - nothing stored. Watchpoint presents a short-lived assertion and you configure (and can revoke) the trust on your side. Prefer this wherever the vendor offers it.
  * `client_credentials` - the one mode that stores a credential. The credential lives in a `watchpoint_vault_secret` and is named here by `credential_secret_key`, never inlined.
  * `mtls` / `local` - the fetch happens on a host inside your network; the certificate or vendor agent never reaches Watchpoint.

Not every vendor supports every mode; the API rejects an unsupported combination on apply.

### Optional

- `allow_browse` (Boolean) Allow listing secret NAMES in this vault, for the portal's picker. Off by default: enumerating needs a wider grant on the vendor's side than fetching does, and a secret name is itself disclosure. Only accepted for vendors whose adapter implements listing.
- `config` (Map of String) Per-vendor non-secret settings, for example `vault_uri` for Azure, `region` and `role_arn` for AWS, `address` and `mount` for HashiCorp Vault. The exact keys a vendor needs are listed on the External Vaults screen in the portal. Nothing secret belongs here.
- `credential_secret_key` (String) The KEY of a `watchpoint_vault_secret` holding the credential. Only valid with `token_source = "client_credentials"`, and required there; every other mode must leave it empty. This is a name, not a value, so it is safe in state.
- `resolution` (String) `control-plane` (default) fetches from Watchpoint. `agent` hands out the reference instead so the secret is fetched inside your network and never transits Watchpoint at all. Required for vaults that are not routable from the internet, and stronger anyway.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Connection ID.
- `last_check_ok` (Boolean) Whether the last test authenticated successfully.
- `last_checked_at` (String) When this connection was last tested (RFC 3339). Cleared on every save, because a green tick measured against a configuration that no longer exists is worse than none.
- `last_error` (String) The vendor's own message from the last failed test.
- `updated_at` (String) Last-update timestamp (RFC 3339).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported by SLUG, not by id: the slug is what the API addresses a connection by
# and what every stored secret reference points at.
terraform import watchpoint_external_vault.aws prod-aws
```
